  • Gwich'in↗historical and present
    Connection & source
    historical and present

    History explicitly connects ancestral lands and continuing relatives/communities with Yukon. No totals adopted.

    Historical homeland and continuing community links. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Han↗Historical homeland connection
    Connection & source
    Historical homeland connection

    Our history locates Hän speakers in western Yukon and eastern Alaska and distinguishes Tr'ondëk Hwëch'in as one group. The existing profile label Han is retained for routing.

    Hän-speaking communities in historical account, including nineteenth century. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Ta'an Kwäch'än↗Community described ancestral territory / government location
    Connection & source
    Community described ancestral territory / government location

    The Council locates ancestral lands around Lake Laberge and neighbouring Yukon/Teslin/Takhini waterways, and explicitly places its headquarters in Whitehorse, Yukon Territory. Inspection: Tàa’an Män section and final paragraph under Final and self-government agreements; surrounding history read. Limits: Broad Yukon route, not a drawn boundary or settlement-land/jurisdiction claim. Percentages of citizens' residence and land-area/legal details not reproduced.

    Ancestral Lake Laberge area and present Whitehorse headquarters described by the Council. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Tagish↗Documented historical language geography
    Connection & source
    Documented historical language geography

    The Centre explicitly identifies the Tagish language with the southern lakes area of Yukon. This adopts the historical geographic connection only; the older page's speaker and school-program descriptions are not current claims.

    Public content inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Tr'ondëk Hwëch'in↗historical and present
    Connection & source
    historical and present

    Nation's history directly identifies Yukon ancestral territory and Tr'ondëk Hwëch'in as a distinct Hän group. Not all Hän people are this government.

    Ancestral territory and present government account. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Tutchone↗Specific language community within broader entry
    Connection & source
    Specific language community within broader entry

    The Centre explicitly locates Southern Tutchone in southwestern Yukon. This supplies one part of the broader Tutchone entry, preserving the distinction from Northern Tutchone and avoiding current speaker or program claims.

    Public content inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Vuntut Gwitchin↗Community described homeland / home community
    Connection & source
    Community described homeland / home community

    The Nation directly locates its homeland in northern Yukon and Old Crow at its heart, and uses Van Tat Gwich’in for the people. Inspection: Opening two paragraphs; protected-area and heritage-route paragraphs also read for scope. Limits: Reference to the Alaska and Northwest Territories borders is not evidence for additional regions. No boundary geometry or protected-area legal interpretation adopted.

    Longstanding homeland and present Old Crow community. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗

These are starting lists, not a complete census. Modern borders help you navigate; they are not Indigenous homeland boundaries. A connection may be historical or present-day and does not imply presence throughout a region. Directory names can overlap; the profiles explain their relationships.
